title: Introduce compact stability ledger and change-contextualizer for snapshot diffs
author: Anika Rao
description: Motivation and summary: Large snapshot onboarding produced verbose profile blobs and brittle release notes; this PR provides a compact, append-only 'stability ledger' designed to store sparse stability signals and provenance per snapshot plus a change contextualizer that synthesizes concise release briefs from ledger deltas and sampled eval signatures. Implementation highlights: ledger implementation in registry/ledger/stability.py introduces a tight binary+JSON entry format keyed by snapshot hash ribbon (sha256_base58). Each entry keeps stability_token (low/medium/high), a small latency_histogram_bucketed summary, token_error_rate as a fixed-point string, and a truncated provenance string; typical entry size is <1KB. The diff serializer at registry/snapshots/diff_serializer.py emits compact delta blobs containing tensor fingerprints, model config deltas, and profile delta summaries (throughput, p50, p95). The serializer supports streaming ingestion and resumable uploads and uses streamed sha256 fingerprinting with an LZ4 compression path. The contextualizer in tools/changelog/contextualizer.go reads ledger deltas and sampled eval signatures and generates prioritized 2-4 sentence briefs that call out regression windows, likely causes, and suggested mitigation actions (e.g., try q4 quantization or revert specific tokenizer changes). Migration and rollout: scripts/migrate_ledger.sh provides an idempotent offline compaction pass that converts legacy verbose snapshot metadata into ledger entries; it is safe to run on read-replicas and gated to registry-admin IAM. The feature is behind registry.features.compact_ledger and will be enabled first for model-registry-internal and a small customer cohort for two weeks before broad rollout. Backwards compatibility: new lightweight API endpoint /snapshots/{id}/ledger returns the compact ledger entry alongside existing full profile for opt-in clients; no breaking changes to existing endpoints. Performance and security considerations: entries are intentionally small to remain indexable in our metadata DB; serializer uses streamed hashing and LZ4 to reduce upload cost; provenance strings are sanitized and truncated to avoid PII, and migration requires elevated IAM. Tests and verification: unit tests added: tests/test_stability_ledger.py and tests/test_diff_serializer.py. Integration harness in benchmark-lab/fixtures/snapshot-churn simulates heavy snapshot churn and validates brief quality metrics. Commits: commit 9a1f2d8 adds ledger core and serializer, commit 3c4b7a1 adds contextualizer and go bindings, commit e2b6c55 adds migration script and tests. Files changed at a glance: registry/ledger/stability.py, registry/snapshots/diff_serializer.py, tools/changelog/contextualizer.go, scripts/migrate_ledger.sh, docs/registry/ledger.md, tests/test_stability_ledger.py, tests/test_diff_serializer.py, benchmark-lab/fixtures/snapshot-churn/seed.yaml, tools/ci/ledger_pipeline.yml, examples/onboard/compact-ledger-example.json, Makefile updates. Review discussion summary: Marcus requested deterministic fingerprinting and a terse entry schema; author clarified the streamed sha256 approach and added a compatibility shim. Sofia asked for privacy guarantees; added sanitization and a note in docs. Devon requested a rollout plan and metrics; added brief_quality and storage_savings metrics and a gated flag. CI: initial run showed a flaky integration test in the harness; rerun after increasing ingestion throttles passed all checks. Merge details: approved by reviewers and merged via squash-merge to main. Release notes: "Add compact stability ledger and contextual changelog generator for snapshot diffs; opt-in API endpoint /snapshots/{id}/ledger; migration script for converting legacy snapshot metadata; feature gated behind registry.features.compact_ledger." Rollout checklist: feature flag, enable internal cohort, monitor brief_quality >=0.85 and storage savings >=40% over legacy blobs, then enable for all. Additional notes: contextualizer is intentionally conservative and surfaces suggestions, not automated rollbacks; storage team consulted on index sizing and approved columnar entry plan.
